sb_prompt: FIND OUT WHAT THE OTHER CALLER DOES IN THE WAY OF LAWN AND GARDEN WORK.DOES THE OTHER CALL ENJOY DOING IT?  COMPARE THIS TO YOUR OWN SITUATION.
raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hello!
ParticipantB: Hello!
ParticipantA: How are you doing?
ParticipantB: Pretty good, just busy. What's up with you?
ParticipantA: I'm good, just wrapping up a shift at the grocery store. I'm the manager here.
ParticipantB: Oh, really? Nice. I work as a pharmacist.
ParticipantA: Oh, wow. That sounds... pretty serious.
ParticipantB: Yeah, it is. Lots of responsibility. But honestly, I've got my hands in a couple of different things lately.
ParticipantA: Like what?
ParticipantB: Well, besides the pharmacy, I've been trying to get my backyard looking better. It's a bit of a mess.
ParticipantA: Oh, that's cool. So you're doing the landscaping yourself?
ParticipantB: Yeah, mostly. I'm trying to figure out how to get some flowers in there without killing them.
ParticipantA: Haha, right? The flowers are tricky sometimes. I've tried to plant things in my own yard, but honestly, I feel like I just make things worse.
ParticipantB: Really? What have you tried?
ParticipantA: Well, last year I got some advice from a neighbor and planted these big bushes around the edge. I thought they'd look nice.
ParticipantB: Oh, did they?
ParticipantA: They didn't. They just took over and choked everything else out. I had to rip most of them out.
ParticipantB: Oh, no. That's frustrating. I've been afraid of doing that to my own garden.
ParticipantA: Yeah, I feel like maybe I'm just not cut out for it. I guess I'm too skeptical about it.
ParticipantB: I get that. I was pretty excited about gardening too, but my brother tried it last summer and it was a disaster.
ParticipantA: Oh, really? What happened?
ParticipantB: He bought all these fancy seeds online and followed the instructions perfectly, but nothing grew. He said the soil was just bad or something.
ParticipantA: Yeah, I felt that way too. Like, why do I keep messing up? Maybe I just have a black thumb or whatever they call it.
ParticipantB: Maybe it's just bad luck. Or maybe we need a pro to show us what we're doing wrong.
ParticipantA: I guess. Though, honestly, I'm kind of relieved I don't have to deal with it. My wife handles all the outside stuff.
ParticipantB: Oh, that's nice. Having someone else do the heavy lifting. I'm still trying to figure out if I even enjoy it enough to keep going.
ParticipantA: I think a lot of people say they love it, but in reality, they just want a nice lawn and don't actually enjoy the work.
ParticipantB: That's true. I don't think I'll be able to keep this up if it gets too much work.
ParticipantA: Yeah, probably not. It's too much time commitment.
ParticipantB: Right. I'll probably just hire someone to do it next time.
ParticipantA: Yeah, that might be the best option.
ParticipantB: For sure. Well, I'm glad we talked about it. I feel like I learned something, even if I'm not doing it myself.
ParticipantA: Yeah, same here. Nice talking to you.
ParticipantB: You too. Bye!
ParticipantA: Bye!
